passages.note: Bill status page shows Griffin as Prime sponsor of HB2756, signed by the Governor 06/04/2026.
House Final Reading vote page shows Griffin voted Y on HB2756.

passages.provision_quote: REQUIREMENTS FOR EXTRA HIGH LOAD FACTOR CUSTOMER PAYMENTS TO COVER THE COSTS OF ANY INFRASTRUCTURE IMPROVEMENTS, ADDITIONS OR expansions THAT ARE NECESSARY TO FACILITATE SERVICE TO THE CUSTOMER, WHICH SHALL BE SUPPORTED BY SCHEDULES that are FILED BY THE ELECTRIC PUBLIC SERVICE CORPORATION THAT DEMONSTRATE THE PROTECTION OF NON-extra HIGH LOAD FACTOR CUSTOMERS FROM subsidizing extra-high load factor customers.
passages.note: Enacted text lets the Corporation Commission set terms requiring extra-high-load-factor customers (e.g. data centers) to pay infrastructure costs and shield other customers from subsidizing them, but does not bar cost pass-through outright, require impact assessments or community benefits, or address permitting.

rows.reasoning: Griffin prime-sponsored, voted for, and saw enacted HB2756 (2026), which lets the corporation commission or public power entity establish payment requirements for new extra high load factor customers 'that demonstrate the protection of non-extra high load factor customers from subsidizing extra-high load factor customers.' This shows direction toward shielding residential ratepayers from cost shifts, but the operative text does not bar utilities from passing 'any' costs to residential customers (rung 2's own word), does not require impact assessments or community benefit requirements before approval (rung 3), and does not address permitting speed or public rate-impact transparency (rung 4), so no single rung's full text is matched.
